messages:
From: Elena Park <ep@finorb.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-06-14T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Request: complete purge of prompts/outputs + runtime logs (EU residency)

Hi Olga,

Following our compliance review (attached), FinOrb needs a full purge of all prompt inputs, generated outputs, and inference runtime logs tied to our account in the EU region. We need:  
- Deletion of prompt & output artifacts stored in object stores and any prompt-output caches;
- Expunge of transient KV cache / LRU entries used by the model runtime;
- Removal of runtime logs (request/response traces) and the index entries that tie logs to user ids;
- Confirmation artifacts for audit: timestamped manifest and hashes where possible.

Our compliance deadline is EOD 2028-06-15 UTC — can you confirm Redwood can perform the purge and provide a completed audit_manifest? Also let us know estimated downtime or service impact (if any).

I've attached the signed deletion form. Please cc legal@finorb.com on the confirmation.

Thanks,
Elena Park
Director of Data Governance
FinOrb Analytics

Attachment: FinOrb_Deletion_Form.pdf (form, signed)

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2028-06-14T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: complete purge of prompts/outputs + runtime logs (EU residency)

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear note and the signed form.

Short answer: yes, we can run a full purge for your EU tenant and provide an audit manifest. Plan and next steps below.

Planned steps (high-level):
1) Verify account scoping (account id + resource mapping) — Marcus to provide the list of S3 prefixes and runtime clusters.
2) Lock new writes for the scoped tenant (soft freeze) to avoid new artifacts during sweep.
3) Run KV cache eviction and clear in-memory checkpoints for active GPUs.
4) Sweep persistent storage (S3, DB indexes, any logs in object buckets) with retention-exempt delete jobs.
5) Run internal validation (hash presence/absence checks) and produce audit_manifest_finorb_20280615.csv.
6) Share manifest + redaction evidence and mark the tenant as completed.

Impact: We aim for zero customer-facing downtime; there may be short (<10s) throttles on the dedicated inference pools during checkpoint clears. We'll highlight any change in the hourly updates.

Would it work for Redwood to run the sweep tonight (2028-06-14) starting 22:00 UTC with final confirmation tomorrow afternoon (2028-06-15)? If that schedule is acceptable I'll kick off the mutual action plan and attach our confirmation template.

Attached: purge_confirmation_template.docx

—Olga

Olga / Marcus — quick ops notes and checklist for the run. I'm pasting the commands and the verification steps we'll run to avoid surprises.

Pre-reqs:
- Confirm account mapping: account_id FIN-77821 -> s3://redwood-prod-eu/tenants/finorb/ and redis prefixes finorb:kv:*.
- Confirm no active long-running batch jobs writing to the tenant buckets.

Execution steps (ops):
1) Mark tenant writes as read-only in routing layer (routing flag: tenant.finorb.read_only = true).
2) Flush Redis keys: redis-cli --scan --pattern "finorb:kv:*" | xargs redis-cli DEL (run on replica after snapshot).
3) Drop model-serving in-memory KV checkpoints: servicectl restart redwood-runtime --tenant finorb --clear-kv (rolling across GPUs).
4) Delete S3 artifacts: aws s3 rm --recursive s3://redwood-prod-eu/tenants/finorb/prompts --quiet; same for /outputs and /logs. Use lifecycle tags to double-remove objects in Glacier classes if any.
5) Remove DB index entries: DELETE FROM inference_logs WHERE tenant_id = 'FIN-77821'; (run in a transaction with export to tmp dump for verification).
6) Produce CSV manifest with paths deleted and SHA256 placeholders where available.

Validation (post-run):
- Smoke test: send 3 quick inference requests (synthetic) and ensure matching tenant id logs are not created.
- Confirm object counts at s3://redwood-prod-eu/tenants/finorb/ are zero.
- Upload audit_manifest_finorb_20280615.csv to secure drive and share link with customer.

Estimated wall-clock: 45-90 minutes depending on object counts. We'll try the 22:00 UTC start. Marcus — can you supply the exact S3 prefixes and estimated object counts so we can confirm window?

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Head of Platform Operations, Redwood Inference

Elena / FinOrb legal —

Per the run we started 2028-06-14 22:00 UTC, Redwood has completed the scoped purge for account FIN-77821 in the EU region. Summary and artifacts below.

What we removed:
- All prompt and generated-output objects under s3://redwood-prod-eu/tenants/finorb/{prompts,outputs,logs} — verified zero objects after run.
- Redis KV entries matching finorb:kv:* flushed from both primary and replica clusters.
- Runtime checkpoints cleared from serving hosts (rolling restarts completed), no residual KV snapshots found.
- Inference logging entries removed from primary DB for tenant_id = 'FIN-77821'.

Evidence delivered: audit_manifest_finorb_20280615.csv (attached) — contains deleted-object paths, deletion timestamps, and SHA256 verification hashes where available. We also uploaded the manifest to a secure link: https://drive.redwood.com/open?id=1xRunbookPurgeEU (access limited to your legal and our compliance team).

Impact: No customer-facing downtime was observed during the operation; we saw short throttling windows (2–8s) during rolling checkpoint clears.

Next steps for FinOrb:
- Please review the manifest and reply to this thread to confirm acceptance of completion.
- If you need notarized evidence or additional hashing proofs, let us know and we'll coordinate an extended report.

Attachments: audit_manifest_finorb_20280615.csv

Thanks — let us know if anything else is required.

Best,
